text: Sora is a town and municipality located in the Central Boyacá Province, within the Colombian Department of Boyacá. It is bordered by Motavita and Chíquiza to the north, Cucaita and Samacá to the south, Motavita and the department capital Tunja to the east, and Sáchica and Chíquiza to the west.[1] The name Sora originates from the Chibcha language and translates to "Devil worshipper."[2] Prior to the Spanish conquest, the region was inhabited by the Muisca, who were part of the loose Muisca Confederation, and Sora was governed by the zaque based in nearby Hunza. Modern Sora was officially established on August 12, 1556, by Tomás Gualba Castellanos.[1] Its geographical coordinates are 5°34′N 73°26′W, or 5.567°N 73.433°W.
